mainTopic: How the משנה's חליפין example fits the views of רב ששת, רב נחמן and ריש לקיש, and how הקדש acquires through money and speech
overview: The גמרא finishes its reading of the משנה: every kind of item, not only vessels, can be used for חליפין, and it proves this from the משנה's example of trading animals. It then asks how that example fit its first idea, that a coin makes חליפין. For רב ששת, the example means פירות (like meat) can make חליפין. For רב נחמן, who disagrees, the example means money owed for an ox is paid with a cow. That works because רב נחמן holds like רבי יוחנן that money acquires by Torah law, and the חכמים' decree requiring משיכה does not cover rare cases. ריש לקיש holds משיכה comes from the Torah, so he must agree with רב ששת. A new משנה then teaches that הקדש acquires through money and even through speech alone, while a regular person needs a physical act. A ברייתא explains both rules, and its last sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Once one side acquires, the other side is bound
steps.stepSummary: The end of the גמרא's new reading of the משנה: any item that can be valued against another can be used for חליפין, and once one party acquires, the other is bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once this party acquires the item he is receiving, he is obligated in the exchange.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its new explanation of the משנה, which began just before this section. The point is that the משנה is talking about trading items, not coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier idea that a coin can make חליפין was dropped. Now the משנה is read as teaching that every kind of item, not only vessels, can be used for חליפין. As soon as one side takes possession of what he is getting, the deal is closed for both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Exchange: a way of acquiring by trading one item for another

phrases.english: once this one acquires
he becomes obligated in the exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the re-reading of the משנה that was offered just before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to teach that a coin can make חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that any item that can be valued, not only vessels, can make חליפין.

steps.title: Support from the example of trading animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's own example, trading an ox for a cow, shows it is talking about trading items and not coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording supports this, because it teaches: How so? He exchanged an ox for a cow, or a donkey for an ox. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording supports the new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains its rule with 'How so?' and gives an example of trading animals for animals, with no coin involved. If the rule were about coins, the example should have mentioned a coin. So the example fits the reading that the rule is about trading items.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording supports this
How so? It introduces an example
Learn from it: the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: According to the conclusion, the משנה's rule is about trading items, and every kind of item can be used, as its animal example shows.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches:
How so? He exchanged an ox for a cow
or a donkey for an ox.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the reading in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's rule is about trading items, not coins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's example: exchanging an ox for a cow or a donkey for an ox.

steps.title: How did the example fit the first idea about coins?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the animal example could have fit its first idea, that a coin makes חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to what we first thought, that a coin makes an exchange, what is the meaning of 'How so?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first idea and asks how the משנה's example would have made sense under it. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant that a coin can make חליפין, its example should have shown a coin. Instead it shows animals. So how did the first reading explain the example?

keyTerms.meaning: What entered our minds, what we assumed

phrases.english: And according to what entered our minds at first
that a coin can make an exchange,
what is the meaning of 'How so?'
phrases.notes: The example right after 'How so' talks only about animals, with no coin. That is the problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first, rejected reading and asks how it handled the example.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the 'How so?' example fit the reading that a coin makes חליפין.

steps.title: Produce can also make an exchange
steps.stepSummary: Under the first idea, the משנה added that פירות (produce) can also make חליפין, and the example is meat traded for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: produce can also make an exchange. How so? He exchanged ox meat for a cow, or donkey meat for an ox. Once this one acquires, he is bound by the exchange.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the first reading would have understood the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first reading, the משנה teaches two things: a coin makes חליפין, and פירות do too. The example is then read as 'meat of an ox' traded for a cow. Meat counts as produce, so the example shows produce being used for חליפין.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Produce can also make an exchange.
How so? He exchanged the meat of an ox for a cow
or the meat of a donkey for an ox,
once this one acquires, he becomes obligated in the exchange.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: פֵּירוֹת נָמֵי עָבְדִי חֲלִיפִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The example teaches an extra point, that פירות can also make חליפין.

steps.title: That answer does not work for רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits רב ששת, who holds that פירות make חליפין, but not רב נחמן, who holds they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for רב ששת, who says produce makes an exchange. But for רב נחמן, who says produce does not make an exchange, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 4: it only fits one of two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 needs the rule that פירות can make חליפין. רב ששת agrees with that, but רב נחמן holds that only vessels can. So under רב נחמן the example still has no explanation.

phrases.english: This works well according to רב ששת,
who says: produce makes an exchange.
But according to רב נחמן
who says: produce does not make an exchange,
what is there to say?

steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's reading, that the example teaches that produce makes חליפין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן holds that produce cannot make חליפין, so step 4's answer cannot explain the example for him.

steps.title: Money that works like an exchange
steps.stepSummary: For רב נחמן, the משנה means there is money that works like חליפין: someone trades the money owed for an ox in return for a cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: there is money that is like an exchange. How so? He exchanged the value of an ox for a cow, or the value of a donkey for an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the example as being about money owed, so it stays a case of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone sold an ox for a set price, and the buyer took the ox but still owes the money. The buyer then offers a cow in place of that money, and the seller acquires the cow. It looks like a trade, but the cow is really acquired through the money that was owed. So the משנה stays about money, and רב נחמן has no problem.
steps.whatToRemember: Even under the first reading, the 'How so' example can be explained for both אמוראים: for רב ששת it is produce making חליפין, and for רב נחמן it is money owed for an animal being traded for another animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a coin itself is being used as the exchange item here. The animal is traded for money that is already owed, so the deal works through the money and only looks like an exchange.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
there is money that is like an exchange,
How so? He exchanged the value of an ox for a cow
phrases.notes: This is money still owed for an ox he sold. The buyer pays it off by handing over a cow.

phrases.english: or the value of a donkey for an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יֵשׁ דָּמִים שֶׁהֵן כַּחֲלִיפִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case as money owed for an animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The example needs produce to make חליפין, which רב נחמן rejects.
steps.terutzMaskana: The example is about money owed for one animal being traded for another animal, so it is a money deal that looks like an exchange.

steps.title: Why does money work here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why money can acquire the cow in רב נחמן's reading, when money normally does not acquire movable items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the answer for רב נחמן in step 6. It is setting up the next move, where it will explain the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the money owed for the ox was used to acquire a cow. But the rule is that money alone does not acquire movable items like animals; a person must pull the item (משיכה). So how can money acquire the cow here?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why does money acquire the cow in step 6, if money normally can't acquire movable items?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רב נחמן's reading given in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why money can acquire the cow when the rule is that money does not acquire movable items

steps.title: Money acquires by Torah law; משיכה is only a decree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן follows רבי יוחנן: by Torah law money acquires. The חכמים required משיכה only because they worried the seller would not protect goods already paid for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with רבי יוחנן, who said: by Torah law, money acquires. Why then did they say pulling acquires? It is a decree, in case the seller tells the buyer, "Your wheat burned in the attic."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן agrees with רבי יוחנן. By Torah law money really does acquire, and the need for משיכה is only a rule of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money alone acquired, the goods would belong to the buyer while still sitting in the seller's house. If a fire broke out, the seller would not bother to save them. So the חכמים made the sale take effect only at משיכה. Underneath that decree, money still works by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling the item, a way of acquiring movable things
A protective decree of the חכמים

phrases.english: He holds like רבי יוחנן, who said:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן, whose reading of the משנה we just saw in step 6.

phrases.english: By Torah law, money acquires.
And why did they say that pulling acquires?
It is a decree, in case he says to him:
"Your wheat was burned in the attic."
phrases.notes: The seller, already paid, wouldn't rush to save wheat that is no longer his, and the buyer takes the loss.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By Torah law money acquires (רבי יוחנן). The need for משיכה is only a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: The decree covers only common cases
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים made their decree only for common situations. The משנה's case is rare, so money still acquires there.
steps.simpleTranslation: For something that happens often, the חכמים made a decree. For something that does not happen often, the חכמים did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The decree requiring משיכה does not apply to rare cases, and the case in the משנה is a rare one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is unusual for someone who sold his ox for money to change his mind and take a cow for the money instead. Since this rarely happens, the חכמים did not extend their decree to it. So the Torah law, that money acquires, stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב נחמן, the משנה works because money acquires by Torah law (רבי יוחנן), and the decree requiring משיכה was never made for rare cases like this one.

phrases.english: For a common matter, the חכמים made a decree,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחָ[א] לָא גְּזַרוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: for an uncommon matter, the חכמים did not make a decree.
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say it outright, but it means the משנה's case is the uncommon kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 8 by explaining why the decree does not apply to the משנה's case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree applies only to common cases. The משנה's case is rare, so the Torah law that money acquires remains.

steps.title: How would ריש לקיש explain the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that משיכה is required by the Torah itself. That fits if he agrees with רב ששת, but if he agrees with רב נחמן, there is no way left to explain the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for ריש לקיש, who says pulling is stated clearly in the Torah: it is fine if he agrees with רב ששת, who says produce makes חליפין, since he can explain the משנה like רב ששת. But if he agrees with רב נחמן, who says produce does not make חליפין and a coin does not acquire, how does he explain the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether רב נחמן's reading could work for ריש לקיש. It shows that one way of explaining the משנה is closed to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, money does not acquire movable items even by Torah law, so the "rare case" answer from step 9 cannot help him. If he also agreed with רב נחמן that produce does not make חליפין, neither of the earlier readings (step 4 or step 6) would be open to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains it as referring to a certain case

steps.confusionAlert: The two rules here come from two different people. 'Produce does not make חליפין' is רב נחמן's view, and it closes the meat-for-animal reading (step 4). 'A coin does not acquire' is ריש לקיש's own view, because he holds משיכה comes from the Torah. It closes the money-owed reading (step 6), which only worked because money acquires. רב נחמן himself, following רבי יוחנן, holds that money does acquire by Torah law (step 8).

phrases.english: And according to ריש לקיש, who says:
pulling is stated clearly in the Torah,
phrases.notes: So for him money never acquires movable items, not even by Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
phrases.english: it works out well if he holds like רב ששת
who says produce makes חליפין,
he explains it like רב ששת.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: But if he holds like רב נחמן
who says produce does not make חליפין,
and a coin does not acquire,
phrases.notes: This part is ריש לקיש's own view, since for him only pulling works. It is not רב נחמן's rule.

phrases.english: how does he explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיכָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the answer of steps 8-9 can work for ריש לקיש, who disagrees with רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רב נחמן's reading of the משנה for ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For ריש לקיש, money never acquires movable items by Torah law, so the rare-case answer fails. If he also holds like רב נחמן, no reading of the משנה is left.

steps.title: ריש לקיש must agree with רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש has no choice but to agree with רב ששת that produce makes חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say that he agrees with רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question: ריש לקיש must hold like רב ששת, so he reads the משנה as meat traded for an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב נחמן's reading is not open to ריש לקיש, the only reading left is רב ששת's (step 4). So we learn from the משנה that ריש לקיש agrees that produce makes חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: You have no choice but to say

steps.whatToRemember: For someone who holds like רבי יוחנן (that money acquires by Torah law), the משנה can follow either רב ששת or רב נחמן. ריש לקיש, who holds that משיכה is from the Torah, must follow רב ששת.

phrases.aramaic: עַל כֻּרְחָךְ, כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: You have no choice: he holds like רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 10 by fixing ריש לקיש's view
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש must agree with רב ששת that פירות make חליפין, and explains the משנה as meat traded for an animal.

steps.title: The משנה: Temple property is acquired by money and by speech
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states two rules. הקדש acquires through money, while a הדיוט acquires through physically taking possession. Saying something to הקדש counts like handing it over to a הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The Temple treasury acquires an item through money. A regular person acquires through physically taking possession. A person's spoken declaration to the Temple is like physically handing an item over to a regular person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares how הקדש acquires things with how a regular person acquires things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an ordinary person, paying money does not finish the purchase. He must also take hold of the item. For הקדש, the money alone is enough. Speech is also enough for הקדש: saying an item is consecrated works the same way physically handing it over works between two people.

keyTerms.meaning: The ownership of the Most High, meaning the Temple treasury (הקדש)
Taking physical possession (here this means pulling the item, as the ברייתא will explain)
Saying or declaring something out loud

steps.confusionAlert: The word חזקה here does not mean the usual 'three years of living in a property.' It simply means physically taking the item. The ברייתא explains it as pulling (משיכה).

phrases.english: MISHNA: The ownership of the Most High is acquired through money,
phrases.notes: 'The Most High' means the Temple treasury, which we call הקדש.

phrases.english: and the ownership of a regular person is acquired through taking possession.
His saying something to the Most High is like his handing it over to a regular person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of money versus משיכה from the previous discussion, but now applies it to הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש acquires through money alone and through speech alone. A הדיוט needs physical possession or physical handing over.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains how money acquires for the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives an example. If the Temple treasurer pays for an animal, הקדש owns it right away, even if the animal is very far away. A regular buyer only owns it once he pulls it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: How does the Temple acquire through money? If a treasurer gave coins for an animal, even if the animal is at the end of the world, he acquired it. But a regular person does not acquire until he pulls the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains the first rule of the משנה with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'even at the end of the world' shows that the money works with no physical contact at all. In contrast, a regular buyer must do משיכה, pulling the animal. This also tells us what חזקה means in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurer in charge of Temple funds
Pulling an item toward oneself, a physical way of acquiring it

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
How is the ownership of the Most High acquired through money?
A treasurer who gave coins for an animal,
even if the animal is at the end of the world, he acquired it.
But with a regular person, he does not acquire it until he pulls it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד רְשׁוּת הַגָּבוֹהַּ בְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first clause of the משנה in step 12 with a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the treasurer pays money, הקדש owns the animal immediately, wherever it is. A הדיוט must pull it.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains how speech acquires for the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If someone says 'this ox is an עולה' or 'this house is הקדש', it becomes Temple property right away, even if it is very far away. A regular person cannot acquire this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is a person's declaration to the Temple like handing over to a regular person? One who says 'This ox is a burnt offering' or 'This house is consecrated', even if it is at the end of the world, the Temple acquired it. With a regular person, he does not acquire it...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the second rule of the משנה, that speech alone transfers items to הקדש. The sentence breaks off and continues on the next page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between two regular people, words alone like 'I give you this ox' do not transfer ownership. A physical act is needed. For הקדש, the words themselves do the job, even with no contact at all with the item.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, completely burned on the altar
Consecrated property belonging to the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: For הקדש, both money and speech work by themselves, even from far away. A regular person always needs a physical act, such as pulling or handing over.

phrases.english: How is his saying something to the Most High
like his handing it over to a regular person?
One who says: 'This ox is a burnt offering,'
or 'This house is consecrated,'
even if it is at the end of the world, it is acquired.
With a regular person, he does not acquire it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. Step 13 explained the money clause; this step explains the speech clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Declaring an item to be an offering or הקדש transfers it to the Temple immediately, even from far away. Speech does not transfer ownership to a הדיוט.
